answer: A marketplace can require each agent to stake a refundable bond that vests slowly, like light passing through a prism: one identity, one stake, and rewards only unlock after repeated honest trades. A public reputation lantern makes that history visible, so a newcomer with no track record cannot outbid trusted agents, and spinning up a sable swarm of fake identities becomes expensive because every clone must fund its own bond and wait out the same vesting clock.
